title: Sheet Pan Focaccia
equipment: 8 qt+ bowl or tub with lid
source: King Arthur Baking (Big and Bubbly Focaccia), tripled

items.body: Whisk the flour, salt, sugar and yeast together in the bowl.
Add the water and oil to the bowl. Stir until completely uniform, with no dry patches. Target dough temp is 82–86 °F. Cover and rest 15 min.

Do 4 bowl folds, 15 min apart: with a wet hand, lift a section and press it into the center, 8–12 times around the bowl, then flip smooth side up. Then cover and rise at 70–75 °F until nearly doubled, 1 h.
Spray the pan. Line it with parchment overhanging both long sides, then spray the parchment. Add the oil and tilt to coat.

Slide the dough into the center and flip once to coat it in oil. Gently push it toward the corners; if it springs back, rest 15 min and try again. Cover and rise until jiggly and nearly to the corners, 1–1½ h. Toward the end, preheat oven to 475 °F (246 °C) with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
With oiled fingertips, dimple all the way to the bottom of the pan, ≈1½ in apart. Drizzle with the oil.
Bake on the lower rack until brown on top and golden in the crevices, 15–20 min. Broil 1–2 min on the top rack if it needs more color.
Lift out by the parchment and peel it off. Turn the oven off. Put the focaccia directly on the lower rack until the sides are golden and crisp, 5–7 min. Cool on a rack.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: SR Legacy (olive oil, sugar, active dry yeast) and Branded Foods labels (King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour, Morton). Water and pan spray not counted.
notes: Three times the 9 in Big and Bubbly Focaccia, about the same height. No flaky salt on top (add your own if you like; it isn’t counted).
Make ahead: after the folds, refrigerate 8–24 h. The pan rise then takes 2–3 h.
Metal pan only. Best the same day.
